evidence.note: Falsifiable claim: the lane sheet can name the step that killed a stopped lane (last_event_kind + mid_gate) instead of 'reason unknown', and recover_auto.decide can classify an expired lease+salvageable worktree as alone-settleable while refusing adopted/operator-answer/unmeasurable. Refuting observation: a lane with no gate event has a non-empty mid_gate. Probe: tests/test_lanes_watchdog.py (synthetic corpses) asserting last_event_kind/mid_gate/remedy and decide() effects; runs FAIL pre-fix (fields absent) and PASS with them.

Followed r-small-files, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-untrusted-data (mid_gate/last_event_kind read from events as data, remedy passed through safe()), r-derive-dont-store (ledger stays a pure function of events+state). Recorded recovery_auto as a pure module with no I/O.

Extended services/lanes ledger Lane with last_event_kind/mid_gate/remedy; _scan + _mid_gates + remedy_for; new services/lanes/recover_auto.py pure decision; advise _resume + render_ledger surface the remedy; committed on ddflow/lanes-watchdog (e7f9526e1, 8556b60a0, 8ba9e4505, 05a48e829). 7 files.

Rubber-duck review of the change: confirm _mid_gates keeps only the latest gate.started with no later outcome (a prior concluded round is not mid-run); confirm remedy_for returns '' for done/live lanes; confirm decide() checks adopted and operator_answer BEFORE salvageable so neither is ever auto; confirm render appends ONE line per stopped lane (safe()-flattened) so a hostile name stays one line; confirm Lane new fields are end-appended with defaults so existing positional constructions test_lanes.py still pass.

ruff check + ruff format clean on all changed files (0 issues); pure modules (recover_auto_, remedy_for) no I/O; single definition per concern (safe() shared, one decide() and one remedy_for()); no new deps, no secrets, no new files outside ddflow/services/lanes + tests.

No new bug introduced. Scoped tests: 526 passed / 0 failed from files this item changed (the 6 ci failures are baseline-red on main, bug Be3461fc98e, untouched files). recover_auto.decide guardrail order verified (adopted/operator-answer before salvageable); remedy_for returns '' for done/live lanes.

No duplicate of an existing ddflow feature: recover_auto.decide is new (core/recovery_plan.triage is the recover --all brain; lanes watchdog has no auto-decision today); last_event_kind/mid_gate are new Lane fields; no string/message duplication (single remedy_for, single decide).

chunk_findings.detail: `decisions` documents that “a row’s own `adopted` wins where both exist,” but the implementation is `adopted = bool(r.get("adopted") or adopted_items.get(r["item"]))`. Since `False` is falsy, an explicit row value of `"adopted": False` does not win when `adopted_items` maps that item to `True`. For example, `decisions([{"item": "a", "lane": "l", "salvageable": True, "adopted": False}], adopted_items={"a": True})` returns `STAY`, but it should return `AUTO_RESUME`; the lane is marked not adopted by the row and the worktree is salvageable, so recovery is incorrectly skipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/recover_auto.py:124

chunk_findings.detail: `_mid_gates` uses `""` as the absent-timestamp sentinel and then compares it with event timestamps: `if e.ts >= started.get(e.subject, ("", ""))[0]` and `ended[key] = max(ended.get(key, ""), e.ts)`. `Event.ts` is numeric in this file (the same hunk later does float epoch math on `f.last_ts`), so the first `gate.started` or first gate outcome event for any item raises `TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'str'`. Example input: `_mid_gates([Event("gate.started", subject="item1", ts=1.0, data={"gate":"build"})])` crashes before any lane row is produced.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:_mid_gates

chunk_findings.detail: `_lane` gains a required seventh parameter `mid_gates: dict[str, str]`, but this diff does not update the existing call site, which still passes the previous six arguments. Any lane-sheet render that reaches that call now dies with `TypeError: _lane() missing 1 required positional argument: 'mid_gates'`, so the watchdog cannot build the `Lane` rows claimed by the change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:_lane

chunk_findings.detail: `_lane` anchors the stopped lane’s `mid_gate` with `mid_gates.get(lane.item, "")`, i.e. item-scoped, but the gate that was mid-run for a stopped lane is lane-scoped. Given events for item `job-1`: `Event(lane="build", item="job-1", kind="gate", gate="compile", ts=100)`, then `Event(lane="build", item="job-1", kind="stop", ts=110)`, then `Event(lane="test", item="job-1", kind="gate", gate="run", ts=120)`, `_mid_gates(events)["job-1"]` is `"run"`. The stopped `"build"` lane row therefore gets `mid_gate="run"` even though that lane never reached `run`; it was stopped at `compile`. This misattributes the corpse to the wrong step and can feed the recover-auto decision with the wrong gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:_lane

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion `assert isinstance(RecoverAuto, type)` checks the class object itself, not the verdict returned by `decide`. `RecoverAuto` is imported as a class, so this is always true. The test claims to verify that `decide` serialises a `RecoverAuto` verdict, but a broken `decide` returning a different object with an `as_dict` method still passes; it should be `assert isinstance(d, RecoverAuto)`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lanes_watchdog.py:test_recover_auto_decisions_serialise_every_verdict

chunk_findings.detail: `_resume` puts `lane.remedy` in the stall-reason slot of `lane {name} stopped ({why}) with {item} unfinished`. A stopped lane whose remedy is a recommendation (the field this change adds for per-cause remedies) and whose state is `STOPPED_UNKNOWN` therefore renders as stopped for that recommendation, for example `stopped (re-lease with a marker)`, and never keeps "reason unknown" or "its session ended". The `or` fallback only runs when remedy is empty, so any corpse that already has a remedy loses the reason the resume move was built to report.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/advise.py:34

chunk_findings.detail: `test_six_silent_deaths_are_all_losslessly_recovered` claims every verdict keeps the work, but the stay branch is `or d.effect == STAY`. A decision `effect=STAY`, `auto=False`, `rationale="deleted the worktree and dropped the item"` still passes, so a regressing `decide`/`decisions` that discards adopted, operator-answer, or unmeasurable corpses is reported as lossless. The rows are also hand-built dicts, not the six ledger corpses, so the assertion never sees a real stall reason or remedy.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lanes_watchdog.py:146

chunk_findings.detail: `decisions` documents that a row's own `adopted` wins when both the row and `adopted_items` set the flag, but the line `adopted = bool(r.get("adopted") or adopted_items.get(r["item"]))` does not. Given `{"item": "i", "lane": "L", "adopted": False, "salvageable": True}` and `adopted_items={"i": True}`, `False or True` is true, so the verdict is `stay` / `auto=False` instead of `auto_file_resume`. A row that already measured the tree as not adopted is therefore not auto-resumed, which drops the lossless recovery this watchdog is supposed to file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/recover_auto.py:decisions

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_mid_gates` uses string defaults for numeric event timestamps: `started.get(e.subject, ("", ""))[0]` and `ended.get(key, "")`. The rest of this module treats `e.ts` as numeric (for example `max(h.last_ts, e.ts)` and `now: float` in `_lane`). With any real event stream containing `gate.started` followed by a gate outcome, the first `gate.started` evaluates `e.ts >= ""`, and the first gate outcome evaluates `max("", e.ts)`; both raise `TypeError` in Python 3 (`'>=' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'str'`). Concrete input: `Event(kind="gate.started", subject="item-1", data={"gate":"build"}, ts=1700000000.0)`. This crashes stall-reason computation before any lane sheet row can be rendered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py:_mid_gates

chunk_findings.detail: The mid-gate attribution is item-scoped, not lane-scoped: `_mid_gates(events)` is precomputed once and then selected with `mid_gates.get(lane.item, "")`, so it can only hold one current gate per item. Since `recover_auto` explicitly may re-lease the same item after a corpse, later events for the new lane overwrite that item’s entry. Example: lane A takes item I and enters gate G1, then dies silently; recover_auto re-leases I to lane B, which then enters G2. `_mid_gates(events)` maps I → G2, and building stopped lane A’s row returns `mid_gate=G2` (or "" if the item was closed/cleared), so the corpse names the wrong step instead of G1.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/ledger.py _lane return

chunk_findings.detail: `decisions` says a row's own `adopted` value wins when both the row and `adopted_items` have a value, but the code uses `bool(r.get("adopted") or adopted_items.get(r["item"]))`. A row's explicit `False` does not win over a fallback `True`. Concrete failure: `decisions([{"item": "a", "lane": "l", "salvageable": True, "adopted": False}], adopted_items={"a": True})` returns `STAY` instead of `AUTO_RESUME`, blocking a losslessly recoverable lane. The row value is ignored whenever it is false, contrary to the documented override and the recovery goal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/recover_auto.py:117

chunk_findings.detail: A stopped lane that has both `detail` (the stall reason: last event kind and mid-run gate) and `remedy` only renders the remedy line, because the new branch uses `if ln.remedy: ... elif ln.detail:`. For example, `detail == "last event lease-expired while running gate prune"` and `remedy == "re-lease with marker; resume item auto-filed"` will produce only `  lane-q3: re-lease with marker; resume item auto-filed`; the step that killed the lane is never shown, which defeats the stated reason-anchoring requirement that a corpse names its last step. The change also updates `tests/test_lanes.py` to assert only a line count of 3, so this dropped reason is not caught.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/render.py:47-49

chunk_findings.detail: `_mid_gates` keys only on item plus gate name and keeps whatever run is still open at query time, then `_lane` copies that onto the stopped lane via `mid_gates.get(lane.item)`. It never checks the lane's agent or that the start was still open at that lane's last event. Given worker `lease.renewed` at t=3 on item-1 (then silence, STOPPED_UNKNOWN) and a later `gate.started` from agent "other" on item-1 gate "lint" with no outcome, the corpse row is `mid_gate=lint` and `remedy_for` says it died inside lint and to re-run lint. The same mis-name happens if recovery opens a gate on the item after the death: the sheet blames the corpse for a step it never ran.
chunk_findings.title: _mid_gates

chunk_findings.detail: `decisions` documents that a row's own `adopted` wins when both the row and `adopted_items` are set, but `bool(r.get("adopted") or adopted_items.get(r["item"]))` does not: a false row value is skipped by `or`. Given `{"item": "wave-1", "lane": "L1", "adopted": False, "salvageable": True, "operator_answer": False}` and `adopted_items={"wave-1": True}`, the verdict is `stay` / `auto=False` instead of `auto_file_resume`. A row that already measured the tree as not adopted is refused auto-recovery, so the watchdog does not file the resume the salvageable expired lease requires.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/recover_auto.py:decisions
